newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends lower on old crop, higher new crop.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends lower on old crop, higher new crop.

text.p: WCE canola closed mixed with old crop weakened by commercial long liquidation and the sluggish pace of export sales, traders said.
New crop positions were firm amid talk that next week's key StatsCan plantings report will show lower planned seedings than many had previously anticipated.
July canola finished $1.50 lower at $421.90 with new crop November up $1.50 at $379.20. The July WCE futures crush profit margin rose to -10.67 Tuesday from -12.97 Monday.
Background support came from growing concern about flooding in southern Manitoba.
Wheat, barley, canola and flaxseed are grown in that area with flooding seen most supportive for flaxseed. July flax finished $0.20 higher at $342.80.
Feedgrains were aided by higher CBOT corn in quiet conditions. May feed wheat rose $1.00 to $173.80 while May western barley was up $0.50 to $141.20.
Feed peas ended mixed with October off US$0.50 at US$198.00. October oats ended steady at US$124.00.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
